evidence.note: R-scalability CONFIRMED (622 git spawns in status from recovery scan). Probe: tests/test_git_batch.py with 126 merged stale leases and trees on disk counted 12600 Popen starts before (100 per lease: verdict, healthwatch scan, per-tree default_branch/status/rev-list/merge-base), <=30 after

r-adapters (all git via infra.git in infra/gitbatch.py), r-derived-cache-bounded (RepoFacts lives for one scan, nothing persisted but a local stamp), r-everything-configurable (3 knobs), r-bounded-everything (view caps), r-unavailable-not-pass (unmeasured tree = salvageable None), r-docs-with-the-change (README knob table, upgrade fragments)
ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py RepoFacts; recovery.scan(view=) with budgets; healthwatch shares the scan; brief sweep throttled by worktree.sweep_interval_s; tests/test_git_batch.py 4 pass

chunk_findings.detail: `worktree.sweep_interval_s` defaults to `900`, but its own documentation says `0` sweeps on every brief “as before”. On an upgrade with no new configuration, `brief` will now skip `dispose_finished` for up to 15 minutes after a prior sweep, so leftover worktrees/branches from finished items that would previously have been cleaned on the next brief remain present. This violates the upgrade-safety requirement that a new knob default to the old behaviour [r-upgrade-safe].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/worktree.py:56

chunk_findings.detail: `lease.scan_view_trees_max` defaults to `16`, changing read-only `status`/`brief` behaviour from measuring every stale worktree to reporting any tree beyond 16 as `NOT MEASURED`. For example, with 17 stale leases, `status` after this change reports at least one tree as not measured and treats it as holding work, whereas the pre-change behaviour measured every tree. This is a default-on behaviour change without an old-behaviour default, violating the upgrade-safety requirement [r-upgrade-safe].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/lease.py:117

chunk_findings.detail: The cadence stamp is a plain timestamp file, not a lock or atomic test-and-set. If two brief/status commands run concurrently when the stamp is missing or stale, both can execute `stamp.read_text()` and observe the old/missing value before either `fsio.replace_text()` completes, then both return `True` and both invoke `CL.sweep_finished`. This violates the docstring’s “At most once per `worktree.sweep_interval_s`” and can duplicate the expensive branch-drop sweep (and any branch-delete race) within a single interval.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:_sweep_due

chunk_findings.detail: `on_base` conflates a git error with a valid “not an ancestor” answer and caches the false result. If `sha` is unknown to the repository (for example a stale recovery entry whose commit has been garbage-collected or came from a deleted worktree), `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <base>` exits with 128, not 1; because the code only checks `.ok`, it stores and returns `False`. Thus a caller sees “this commit is not on base” when git actually could not answer, violating the module’s stated “unknown is not zero” invariant and defeating `prefetch_on_base`’s promise that unknown objects are not remembered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py:on_base

chunk_findings.detail: `_prefetch_landed` is called before the per-item loop and ignores both `view` and `_Budget`. It builds `shas` from every non-removed item with `merged_sha` and a passed merge gate, then calls `facts.prefetch_on_base(...)`. For example, with `scan(..., view=True)` and `cfg.lease.scan_view_verdicts_max=0` (or `1`), a state containing 126 non-removed items that each have `merged_sha` and `gate_outcome("merge") == "passed"` still causes `_prefetch_landed` to build a 126-element list and prefetch all 126 landed verdicts. The subsequent `_note_landed` calls can then use the prefetched answers without consuming the verdict budget, so the read-only view can determine more completions than the configured cap and can still perform unbounded/batched git work for that verdict set. This contradicts the docstring’s “weighs at most `lease.scan_view_verdicts_max` completions” and the bounded-cache requirement. [r-bounded-everything] [r-derived-cache-bounded]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py:_prefetch_landed

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_prefetch_landed` call is unconditional, even when no recovery candidate will be measured or weighed. Example: `state` contains one completed item with `removed=False`, `merged_sha` set, `gate_outcome("merge") == "passed"`, no lease, no worktree, and not interrupted. `scan(..., view=True)` will not emit a `Recovery` for that item, but `_prefetch_landed` still calls `facts.base(cfg.worktree.base_ref)` and `facts.prefetch_on_base(...)`, forcing git work for an item that cannot appear in the report. If the base ref is unavailable or git is slow/failing, a read-only status can fail or degrade even though the old scan would have returned an empty recovery list without needing git answers for that state. [r-unavailable-not-pass]
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py:scan

chunk_findings.detail: The note declares `impact = "additive"`, but `new = "900"` changes the old brief behavior. The test changes demonstrate this: `test_finished_tree_sweep` now has to set `worktree.sweep_interval_s=0` in T6/T7/T13 to get the previous “sweep on every brief” behavior. After upgrading, a finished worktree that would previously have been swept on the next `brief` can persist for up to 900 seconds, so the upgrade note misstates the impact and violates the stated conformance that a new knob defaults to the old behaviour [r-everything-configurable].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.worktree.sweep_interval_s.toml:8

chunk_findings.detail: This note also claims `impact = "additive"`, but its own text says status and brief “no longer weigh the full completion of every merged-but-unfinished item” and that setting the new knob above `0` is required to restore that behavior. With the advertised default `new = "0"`, an upgraded repo with merged-but-unfinished items can get status/brief output that omits completion weighing that the old code performed, so this is a behavior change, not an additive knob, and contradicts the “new knob defaults to old behaviour” conformance claim [r-everything-configurable].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_verdicts_max.toml:8

chunk_findings.detail: The change introduces a new git-facing abstraction (`RepoFacts`, `_real`) in `ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py` and wires it into `recovery.py` (the new functions take/use `RepoFacts` and construct `RepoFacts(repo)`). The recorded rule [r-adapters] requires external dependencies such as git/subprocesses to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, with one implementation per function. Putting the real git batch implementation under `ddflow/infra` routes git subprocesses through a new port outside the adapters directory, so callers/tests now depend on infra’s git implementation rather than the adapter port.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py (RepoFacts/_real) [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: The test invokes `LC.brief(repo, agent="reader")` twice but never asserts the returned `exit` value. If `brief` regresses so that it performs two sweeps and then returns a non-zero result (for example because a later cadence/cleanup path breaks after the mocked `sweep_finished` calls), `calls` can still be `2` and the test passes. This is a false-pass path: the adjacent cadence test checks `.exit == 0`, while this one can pass even when the API is unhealthy.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_git_batch.py:test_sweep_interval_zero_sweeps_on_every_brief

chunk_findings.detail: The new scalability test directly spawns real `git` subprocesses and counts them by monkeypatching `subprocess.Popen`, and the manifest adds the git batcher as `ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py` rather than as a port/fake under `ddflow/adapters`. Project guidance r-adapters requires external dependencies such as git/subprocess tools to go through an adapter port and requires tests to use a fake instead of real subprocess spawning; this change violates that guidance.
chunk_findings.title: [r-adapters] tests/test_git_batch.py:_Spawns
